# Lightbridge Provides Business Update and Announces Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Financial Results


November 02, 2026 7:00am EST[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_9b2f83e8d6350e14313010751d324667/ltbridge/news/2026-11-02_Lightbridge_Provides_Business_Update_and_485.pdf)


## Related Documents


[Earnings Webcast Audio](https://edge.media-server.com/mmc/p/tq3xrk6z/)


RESTON, Va., Nov. 02, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation (“Lightbridge” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: LTBR), a nuclear fuel technology company developing Lightbridge Fuel™ to produce more power from existing and new reactors, today reported financial results for the third quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and provided an update on its fuel development activities.


**Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Business Highlights**


- **Lightbridge was selected for the DOE Nuclear Energy Launch Pad INL program.** In August 2026, Lightbridge was selected to participate in the program, which is administered by DOE's National Reactor Innovation Center (NRIC) at Idaho National Laboratory (INL). Selection provides an accelerated pathway toward DOE authorization for the Company to design, build, and operate the Lightbridge Fuel™ Pilot Factory (Pilot Factory), which the Company also refers to as SHED, at INL to manufacture lead test assemblies (LTAs) of Lightbridge Fuel™ for demonstration in U.S. commercial power reactors. The Company is negotiating the applicable agreements and project scope with NRIC and INL. Authorization to construct and operate the Pilot Factory remains subject to additional DOE/INL agreements, reviews, and authorizations.


- **Secured loop irradiation testing of clad fuel rodlets in the Advanced Test Reactor (ATR).** In August 2026, the Company entered into Project Task Statement (PTS) No. 2 under its Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) with Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), the DOE operating contractor for INL. The work covers experimental design, materials, assembly, irradiation, shipment, and disposition of enriched uranium-zirconium fuel rodlets with cladding, in both cylindrical and multi-lobe geometries, irradiated in the ATR loop facility under controlled conditions representative of a commercial reactor.


- **Post-irradiation examination of the first fuel samples is currently underway.** The first batch of Lightbridge Fuel™ material coupon samples, discharged from the ATR on schedule in May 2026, is currently undergoing post-irradiation examination at INL.


- **Expanded patent protection in Japan.** In September 2026, the Japan Patent Office issued a notice of allowance for the Company's multi-zone fuel element patent application, with allowed claims covering the fuel element design, a fuel assembly containing it, and an additive manufacturing method for producing it. Japan operates 32 reactors, 15 of which have returned to service, and its national energy plan targets nuclear at approximately 20% of electricity generation by fiscal 2040.


**Management Commentary**


“Selection for the Launch Pad INL program can help to accelerate our commercialization plan,” said Seth Grae, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge. “Rather than waiting for a commercial fuel factory to be licensed before we could manufacture lead test assemblies, we now have a pathway toward DOE authorization for a dedicated Pilot Factory at INL, and we are negotiating the agreements and project scope with NRIC and INL. In parallel, the loop irradiation agreement we signed in August will enable irradiation testing of the clad Lightbridge Fuel rodlets in the ATR under the conditions similar to those in commercial pressurized water reactors. We believe the loop irradiation will allow us to go from the ATR directly to lead test assemblies in commercial nuclear power plants, rather than first deploying segments of fuel rods and lead test rods in commercial reactors.”


“Our path to acceleration comes at a pivotal moment for the nuclear sector, as major technology companies and utilities increasingly turn to nuclear energy to meet surging baseload power demand from AI, data centers, and industrial electrification. This requires getting substantially more power and higher capacity factors out of the existing nuclear fleet, alongside new builds. Utilities consistently tell us they want three things from an advanced fuel: longer operating cycles between refuelings, power uprates of 10% to 20% from the same plant footprint and operating license, and inherent safety margins that reduce capital and operating costs. Lightbridge Fuel is engineered specifically to meet those requirements.”


**Financial Highlights**


Working capital was approximately $234.2 million at September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $201.7 million at December 31, 2025.


**Cash Flows Summary**


Cash and cash equivalents totaled $236.7 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $201.9 million at December 31, 2025, an increase of $34.8 million. Cash equivalents consisted primarily of U.S. Treasury instruments with maturities of 30 to 90 days.


- Net cash used in operating activities was $13.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $8.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, reflecting higher research and development (R&D) and general and administrative (G&A) spending, partially offset by higher interest income.


- Net cash provided by financing activities was $48.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $121.4 million for the same period in 2025. The Company sold approximately 4.3 million shares of common stock under its at-the-market (ATM) program during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, for net proceeds of $48.9 million, including 579,685 shares for net proceeds of $4.5 million in the third quarter. As of September 30, 2026, approximately $91.4 million of common stock remained available for sale under the Company's $150 million ATM program.


**Third Quarter 2026 Operations Summary**


- G&A expenses were $5.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The $1.8 million increase reflects a $0.9 million increase in employee compensation and stock-based compensation for employees, contractors, and directors, driven by new hires, higher bonuses, and new stock-based awards; a $0.7 million increase in professional and consulting services; and a $0.2 million increase in other administrative expenses, including information technology, insurance, patent, and travel costs.


- R&D expenses were $5.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The $3.3 million increase reflects a $1.9 million increase in employee compensation and stock-based compensation from new hires, higher bonuses, and new stock-based awards; a $1.0 million increase in information technology expenses, primarily computer software and operating costs for the Company's high-performance computer; and a $0.4 million increase in INL project costs as the Company entered into additional agreement modifications and new PTSs.


- Total non-cash stock-based compensation expense was $2.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Stock-based compensation included in G&A was $1.6 million, compared to $1.1 million in the prior-year quarter. Stock-based compensation included in R&D was $0.8 million, compared to $0.5 million in the prior-year quarter.


- Other income was $2.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, consisting of interest income earned on higher cash balances invested primarily in U.S. Treasury bills.


- Net loss was $8.3 million, or $(0.23) per basic and diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of $4.1 million, or $(0.16) per basic and diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025.


**Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 Operations Summary**


G&A expenses were $13.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $9.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The $3.8 million increase reflects a $2.4 million increase in employee compensation and stock-based compensation, a $1.0 million increase in professional and consulting services, and a $0.4 million increase in other administrative expenses.


- R&D expenses were $12.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $5.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The $7.3 million increase reflects a $4.3 million increase in employee compensation and stock-based compensation; a $1.7 million increase in information technology expenses, including software, operating costs for the Company's high-performance computer, and code development; a $0.6 million increase in INL project costs; a $0.4 million increase in project development costs, primarily critical heat flux testing and safety analysis; and a $0.3 million increase in other outside R&D expenses.


- Total non-cash stock-based compensation expense was $6.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Stock-based compensation included in G&A was $4.4 million, compared to $2.7 million in the prior period. Stock-based compensation included in R&D was $1.9 million, compared to $0.9 million in the prior period. The 2026 total stock-based compensation expense included a $0.7 million reversal recorded in the second quarter of previously recognized stock-based compensation for a performance milestone no longer deemed probable of achievement, of which $0.5 million was included in G&A and $0.2 million was included in R&D.


- Other income was $5.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.


- Net loss was $20.4 million, or $(0.62) per basic and diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of $12.4 million, or $(0.55) per basic and diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

**About Lightbridge Corporation**
Lightbridge Corporation (Nasdaq: LTBR) is focused on developing advanced nuclear fuel technology essential to delivering abundant clean energy and providing energy security to the world. The Company is developing Lightbridge Fuel™, a proprietary next-generation nuclear fuel technology for existing light water reactors and pressurized heavy water reactors, significantly enhancing reactor safety, economics, and proliferation resistance. The Company is also developing Lightbridge Fuel for new small modular reactors to deliver the same benefits, plus load-following.


Lightbridge has entered into two long-term framework agreements with Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC, the United States Department of Energy’s operating contractor for Idaho National Laboratory, the United States’ lead nuclear energy research and development laboratory. DOE’s Gateway for Accelerated Innovation in Nuclear program has twice awarded Lightbridge to support the development of Lightbridge Fuel over the past several years. An extensive worldwide patent portfolio backs Lightbridge’s innovative fuel technology. Lightbridge is included in the Russell 2000®, Russell 3000®, and Solactive Global Uranium and Nuclear Components Total Return Indexes.
